properties.description:
Slice 3 of the hub work, the plan as of 2026-10-07.
(1) RECEIVE: a tool, or a field on add_requirement, takes the origin (sending design id, sending requirement id, version) and the sender, and lands the Requirement at proposed with provenance imported. Refused at any other status, so file-only holds wherever the receiver's own rules run.
(2) SEND: in the parent, allocating a requirement to a part's pin records the allocation (which requirement went to which member, when), so the parent can ask later what became of it.
(3) REPORT, in loop_status and upstream_status: requirements received and still proposed, as one inbox; received requirements whose origin moved since they were taken (the existing watch, applied per requirement); and, in the parent, each allocation as the part records it (accepted, dropped, or still waiting), read with arriving_from-style hops from the part.
(4) RIPPLE: a received requirement belongs to the part, so slice 2's continue_in 'down' gets real seeds (the requirements the part received from this parent) instead of empty ones.
(5) /hub: offers to allocate when a parent requirement clearly belongs to one part, and puts the inbox to the part's owner. Where one person owns both, they accept in the same step with their own word.
NOT IN IT: a Decision node crossing (dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs option (b) stays open), and flo2.io enforcing file-only (a flo2 permission level; reflow2 only refuses non-proposed receipts).



RE-PLANNED 2026-10-07 ON ANTHONY'S WORD ("re-plan slice 3 to include Decisions"): DECISIONS TRAVEL THE SAME PATH. A sent Decision arrives at proposed with its origin, and its reasoning travels with it as the node itself, not as text attached to a requirement. Once the receiving owner accepts it, the receiving design's own nodes may be GOVERNED_BY it; that copy is local, so check_intent_authority stays single-owner. A reopened or changed origin decision is reported as moved, like a requirement. Alternatives the decision chose between, which live only in the sender, travel as text. STILL OUT: an enforced DesignRule crossing into the receiver's CI.



═══ REVISED AGAIN 2026-10-07: MOVE OR DECOMPOSE, NEVER COPY ═══
Supersedes the copy-with-origin plan above and the 'decisions travel the same path' re-plan. RECEIVE becomes: a moved requirement (its home changes, the sender keeps a cross-design link), a decomposed piece (the receiver's own requirement, DECOMPOSES to the sender's across designs), or derived requirements from a sender's decision (linked to it). Each lands proposed. The origin-moved report becomes the cross-design link's far-end check. DEPENDS ON cap:a-design-records-a-typed-link-to-a-node-in-another-design-and-reports-when-its-far-end-moves. Build order 5 of 7.



AS BUILT 2026-10-08 (item 5):
- Tools: receive_from_design (receiver) and send_to_design (sender), with kind moved, piece or derived.
- What lands is a proposed Requirement with received_from_design, received_from_node and received_kind, provenance imported, and lineage original, decomposed or derived. It carries DECOMPOSES (piece) or GOVERNED_BY (derived) to the reference standing in for the sender's node, and is refused once its owner has ruled on it.
- In the sender: a move drops the requirement (moved_to_*) with the owner's approver, the reference OBSOLETES it, and the move is refused while a capability here satisfies it. A piece's reference DECOMPOSES the requirement; a derived one's reference is GOVERNED_BY the decision.
- upstream_status lists `received` and `sent`, plus received_waiting per sending design; loop_status names received_waiting.
- The trace check treats a reference child as handed off, not as a gap.
- The ripple carries down seeded at what the part received.
- DECOMPOSES widened (schema/core.yaml), per dec:decomposes-and-governed-by-may-reach-a-cross-design-reference-2026-10-08.
NOT YET: the sender reading the part's acceptance directly. That is the hub agent's read of the part's upstream_status `received`.
properties.name: A design receives a requirement from another design at proposed, with its origin; reports what waits on its owner and what moved at the origin; a parent sees each allocation's status
